County budget execution: budgets, spending, revenue and pending bills

Source: R/county-budget.R
knbs_county_budget.Rd

Each county's approved budget and actual spending, its spending by economic classification, its own-source revenue against target, its pending bills and its exchequer issues, from the Office of the Controller of Budget's annual County Governments Budget Implementation Review Reports, FY 2013/14 to FY 2023/24, for the 47 counties and the national total, with the counties' 2019 census codes.

Usage

knbs_county_budget(fiscal_year = NULL, county = NULL, measure = NULL)

Arguments

fiscal_year

Keep only these fiscal years, such as "2023/24".

county

Keep only these counties, by name or census code, as knbs_county_code() reads them; "00" or "Kenya" for the total.

measure

Keep only these measures.

Value

A knbs_data tibble with columns fiscal_year, geo_code, county, measure, value, unit, status, table_id, printed (the report's table number), pages and source_id. knbs_metadata() gives its provenance; knbs_cite() cites it.

Details

The Controller of Budget's website answers programs with a bot check, which the package does not get past, so these figures ship with the package rather than being read at run time. They were extracted from the reports by curated recipe and verified as every report table is: each county and the total present once, the row identities the tables print (total = recurrent + development) holding on every row, the counties adding up to the printed totals, and figures checked by hand. A copy of a report can be re-read with knbs_report_table() and its file argument.

Measures (measure), money in KSh million:

  • budget_recurrent, budget_development, budget_total: the approved budget estimates.

  • expenditure_recurrent, expenditure_development, expenditure_total: actual spending.

  • absorption_recurrent, absorption_development, absorption_total: spending as a percent of budget, as the reports print them.

  • FY 2014/15 also has exchequer_recurrent, exchequer_development, exchequer_total (funds released by the National Treasury) and spending as a percent of them.

  • FY 2013/14 splits the budget and spending between the County Assembly and the County Executive (budget_assembly, expenditure_executive_total, ...) and has no recurrent/development split of the budget; its overall recurrent, development and total spending and overall absorption are derived from the split and carry status = "derived".

  • Spending by economic classification (all years but FY 2014/15): expenditure_personnel and expenditure_operations_maintenance, and for FY 2013/14 expenditure_debt_pending_bills.

  • Own-source revenue: osr_target, osr_actual (what was collected) and osr_performance (percent of target); by quarter osr_q1 to osr_q4 (FY 2014/15 to 2018/19); and for FY 2019/20 and 2023/24 the split into osr_target_ordinary, osr_target_aia, osr_actual_ordinary and osr_actual_aia. In FY 2023/24 the totals include the facility improvement funds and appropriations-in-aid that earlier years leave out, so use osr_actual_ordinary for a like-for-like series. FY 2013/14 also gives revenue_equitable_share, revenue_conditional_grants and revenue_total_budgeted.

  • Pending bills at 30 June (FY 2014/15 on): pending_recurrent, pending_development, pending_total; from FY 2021/22 also by arm of government (pending_executive_recurrent, pending_assembly_development, ...), with the overall recurrent and development bills derived from them.

  • Exchequer issues by arm of government (FY 2015/16 to 2018/19): exchequer_assembly_recurrent, exchequer_executive_total, ... and the combined exchequer_recurrent, exchequer_development and exchequer_total.

status says how far to trust a figure as it stands:

  • NA: as printed, and consistent with its row and column.

  • "derived": computed as described above.

  • "misprint": printed inconsistently with its own row or column, and kept as printed. FY 2015/16: Busia's total expenditure in the budget table (5,865.76, where its parts sum to 5,896.98) and its personnel cost in the classification table (short by 3 million); the national own-source revenue target (printed 50,539,446 for 50,539,746,840). FY 2022/23: Nairobi's executive recurrent bills (9,000 short).

  • "inconsistent": a total that does not equal its parts, with nothing to show which figure is wrong (Laikipia's pending bills, FY 2020/21).

  • "not_reported": a county the report says did not submit figures, with NA values. Where a report prints a dash for such a county the value is also NA; where a dash means nil it is zero.

Reports do not always agree with themselves. In FY 2015/16 the budget table counts 30 million of Turkana's spending as recurrent and the classification table as development; the budget table's figures are the ones given here. In FY 2013/14, recurrent spending summed from the arms of government differs from personnel plus operations and maintenance. The FY 2019/20 budget table is titled "FY 2018/19" by mistake; its figures are FY 2019/20's. The FY 2024/25 report is not yet included.

See also

knbs_report_table() to read one of the reports' tables from your own copy; knbs_gcp() and knbs_county_population() for county output and population.

Examples

budget <- knbs_county_budget(fiscal_year = "2023/24")
spending <- knbs_county_budget(measure = c("expenditure_recurrent", "expenditure_development"))
knbs_county_budget(county = "Nairobi City", measure = "absorption_development")
